title: Cell Structure
description: The basic unit of life — comparing plant and animal cells and their organelles.

notes.heading: The Cell Theory
notes.body: Three principles: (1) All living things are made of cells. (2) The cell is the basic unit of life. (3) All cells come from pre-existing cells. Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus; prokaryotic cells (bacteria) do not.

notes.heading: Animal Cell Organelles
notes.body: Nucleus: control centre, contains DNA. Cell membrane: controls entry/exit. Cytoplasm: jelly-like fluid for reactions. Mitochondria: produce energy (ATP) — "powerhouse". Ribosomes: make proteins.

notes.heading: Plant Cell Extras
notes.body: Plant cells have three extra structures: cell wall (cellulose, for support), large central vacuole (stores water), chloroplasts (contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis). Plant cells are more box-like and regular.

flashcards.definition: Produce energy (ATP) through respiration — "powerhouse of the cell".
Thin barrier controlling what enters and exits the cell.
Found only in plant cells; contains chlorophyll; site of photosynthesis.
Rigid cellulose layer around plant cells for support.

questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration to produce ATP.

questions.stem: Which structure is in plant cells but NOT animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall for extra support.

questions.stem: Where do new cells come from according to cell theory?
questions.explanation: All cells arise from pre-existing cells through division.

questions.stem: The cell membrane's function is to:
questions.explanation: It is selectively permeable, controlling substance movement.

questions.stem: Key difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound nucleus — DNA floats freely in cytoplasm.
